briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East remains on high alert with a significant fuel price hike in Iran leading to internal security measures and escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Houthi forces continue to strike Saudi Aramco facilities, while Israel and Hezbollah engage in cross-border clashes, resulting in casualties on both sides and reports of civilian deaths in Lebanon. Internationally, the UK is preparing to announce sanctions on Israeli settlements, and the US is actively involved in diplomatic efforts and naval operations related to the Iran conflict.

IRAN
The Iranian government dramatically increased the price of the third tier of gasoline from 5,000 to 10,000 Toman per liter, effective 00:00, 17 Shahrivar (September 7). This has led to reports of crowded gas stations and a heavy security presence with special forces patrolling in cities like Tehran, Mashhad, Rasht, and Karzoun. Opposition sources report the execution of rapper Arfan Mirzaei in Isfahan prison, who was arrested during January protests. There are also reports of protests in Semnan following alleged harassment by Iraqi students.

Militarily, the US Central Command (CENTCOM) claims to have diverted two vessels as part of its naval blockade against Iran. Iran's acting defense minister, Sardar Ebn-al-Reza, stated Iran possesses the capability to strike US warships enforcing the blockade. Major General Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, announced a clear warning from Iran's new missiles and stated that economic warfare will be met by a maritime exclusion zone across the Persian Gulf to the blockade perimeter, with any vessel entering without coordination to be placed on a sanctions list. He also claimed a specific anti-ship missile was tested over a US carrier, forcing it to flee, though US sources imply the USS Abraham Lincoln is in Pattaya, Thailand. Iran's Navy Commander Rear Admiral Shahram Irani reiterated the ability to cripple the enemy anywhere and monitors enemy movements in real time. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf warned that any attack on Iran’s oil and gas assets would draw retaliation against American energy interests in the region. Iran’s Airports and Air Navigation Company reported 27 airports across the country sustained damage during recent aggression.

ISRAEL
The Israeli military conducted operations in Gaza, Lebanon, and the West Bank. In Gaza, the IDF killed two terror operatives: Sabhi Khader al-Hashem al-Batrihi (Palestinian Islamic Jihad) and Ahmad Fuad Khalil Khalas (Hamas Nukhba Force), both involved in planting bombs against Israeli troops. Yusuf Aqila, a Hamas Nukhba company commander, was also killed in Gaza City. The IDF reported killing 14 terror operatives in the Strip in the past week, including five Nukhba company commanders and five Nukhba platoon commanders, noting these actions systematically violated the ceasefire. An IDF engineering vehicle was hit by a Hamas explosive device near the "Yellow Line" in northern Gaza, prompting retaliatory strikes on Hamas infrastructure. The IDF also stated it diverted a munition in mid-air to avoid civilian casualties during a strike on a Hamas operative in Gaza City.

In southern Lebanon, two IDF Golani Brigade reconnaissance soldiers were lightly wounded in a clash near Beaufort Castle with a Hezbollah gunman, who was subsequently killed. The IDF responded by striking Hezbollah weapon depots, command centers, and other terror infrastructure. The IDF also struck Hezbollah operatives moving weaponry in Kfar Remen and several members of the terror group in Nabatieh in response to explosive drone attacks.

In the West Bank, an Israeli settler was severely wounded in a stabbing attack at the Maoz Yehuda settlement farm near Usarin. The Palestinian assailant was located in a nearby village (Idna) and killed by an IDF company commander after attempting to stab soldiers.

Politically, UK plans for sanctions on Israeli settlements have drawn sharp reactions. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for the immediate expulsion of the British Ambassador, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called for Israel to recognize Argentinian sovereignty over the Falkland Islands in retaliation. Coalition talks are ongoing, with parties submitting their lists for the upcoming Knesset elections. Dr. Aliza Bloch joined Blue and White, while MK Michael Biton left the party. Gadi Eisenkot's party "Yasher!" presented its list, including figures like Ohad Ben Ami (released hostage survivor) and family members of fallen soldiers and hostages. The "Hind Rajab Foundation" filed a criminal complaint against Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar in Slovenia for alleged war crimes.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Ground operations included Israeli strikes against terror operatives and infrastructure in Gaza, and a manhunt for a stabber in the West Bank. Casualties in Gaza include 14 terror operatives killed by Israeli strikes in the past week. A Palestinian stabbed an Israeli settler, who is in moderate-to-serious condition, before being killed by IDF forces. ICRC visits for security prisoners in Israeli jails are expected to resume on Wednesday. A US official, according to CBS News, expressed disappointment that Israel has not provided necessary guarantees for a new police force in Gaza, independent of Hamas, and is not fulfilling commitments to allow materials for reconstruction projects. The official also stated that some Israeli airstrikes exceed the right of self-defense and cause insecurity. UK is expected to announce a trade ban on goods from Israeli settlements and sanctions on companies involved in construction in the West Bank.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched two explosive drones at Israeli troops in the Ali Taher Ridge area, causing no injuries. A Hezbollah gunman opened fire on IDF soldiers near Beaufort Castle, wounding two lightly before being killed. In response, Israel carried out extensive airstrikes on Hezbollah infrastructure, including weapon depots and command centers, in southern Lebanon. Lebanese media, specifically the National News Agency, reported 11 people killed and five wounded in Israeli airstrikes overnight in Kfar Reman, including two children and two paramedics. Other strikes hit Nabatieh (where a journalist from Al-Manar was reportedly injured) and Arab Salim, and destroyed a building in Deir al-Zahrani after an evacuation warning. Reports indicate residents are evacuating southern Lebanon due to the intensity of the Israeli attacks.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Syrian Foreign Minister Assad al-Shaibani stated at an Arab League meeting that weapons should be under state control, and armed factions have been integrated into the Syrian army. He also said Damascus opposes Iranian attacks on Gulf States and Jordan and supports a diplomatic solution with Israel. The Syrian FM reported US-mediated talks have begun to stop Israeli attacks on Syrian territory. In Iraq, the Hezbollah-allied Nujaba movement stated they would not surrender their weapons, can organize them, and demand the expulsion of US military forces, expressing solidarity with the Yemeni people against Saudi aggression. Reports from Semnan, Iran, describe clashes at a university dormitory involving Iranian students and Iraqi students (allegedly from Hashed al-Shaabi) following accusations of harassment of an Iranian girl.

GULF STATES
Yemeni Houthi forces launched multiple ballistic missile and drone attacks, striking Saudi Aramco oil facilities in Jizan and the "Abha crude oil station" in Abha for the second consecutive night, with satellite images showing large fires and smoke plumes. A Houthi official warned that Saudi oil, industrial, and vital facilities are no longer safe. Saudi artillery shelled the Al Sheikh area in Yemen's Manbh district. Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al Ahmad Al Sabah and Pakistani counterpart Muhammad Ishaq Dar discussed regional peace efforts. A senior advisor to the UAE President indicated it might take decades to restore trust in Iran. Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesman, discussing ongoing negotiations, highlighted efforts to de-escalate the crisis, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and reduce economic pressure, noting that sanctions have not yielded desired results.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  The UK is expected to announce extensive sanctions on Israeli settlements tomorrow, including a trade ban on products and sanctions on companies involved in construction in the West Bank.
2.  Iran dramatically increased the price of the third tier of gasoline from 5,000 to 10,000 Toman per liter, effective 00:00, September 7, leading to heightened security measures and reports of crowded gas stations across the country.
3.  Yemeni Houthi forces launched multiple drone and missile attacks for the second consecutive night, striking Saudi Aramco oil facilities in Jizan and the Abha crude oil station, causing large fires.
4.  Two IDF soldiers were lightly wounded in a clash with a Hezbollah operative near Beaufort Castle in southern Lebanon; the operative was killed, and the IDF responded with strikes on Hezbollah sites. Lebanese media reported 11 killed in Israeli strikes in Kfar Reman, including two children.
5.  The IDF eliminated a Hamas Nukhba company commander (Yusuf Aqila) and another Hamas Nukhba operative (Ahmad Fuad Khalil Khalas), along with a Palestinian Islamic Jihad member (Sabhi Khader al-Hashem al-Batrihi), in Gaza. A total of 14 terror operatives have been killed in the past week.
6.  A Palestinian assailant stabbed an Israeli settler at the Maoz Yehuda farm in the West Bank, severely wounding him, and was subsequently located and killed by IDF troops.
7.  Iran's security chief, Major General Mohsen Rezaei, announced that Iran will declare a new "restricted maritime zone" outside the Strait of Hormuz in the coming days and warned that any vessel entering without coordination with Tehran would be placed on an Iranian sanctions list.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran threatening a new "restricted maritime zone" and warning against attacks on its energy assets. The ongoing US naval blockade against Iran and US consideration of referring Iran's nuclear file to the UNSC further elevate tensions. Southern Lebanon is an active flashpoint, with direct military clashes between Israel and Hezbollah, involving exchange of fire, drone attacks, and Israeli retaliatory airstrikes resulting in reported civilian casualties, raising the risk of a broader conflict. The Gaza Strip and West Bank remain volatile, with continued Israeli counter-terrorism operations, the stabbing attack on an Israeli settler, and the killing of the assailant. In Yemen, the Houthi's sustained missile and drone attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities and Saudi retaliatory airstrikes, coupled with multi-front fighting, indicate continued instability and potential for regional spillover.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture is complex, with CENTCOM enforcing a naval blockade against Iran, President Trump commenting on the "war with Iran" and potential oil price drops, and other US officials criticizing Israeli actions in Gaza and facilitating talks between Syria and Israel. The US is also reportedly exploring referring Iran's nuclear file to the UN Security Council. Qatar is actively mediating between Iran and the US, working to de-escalate the crisis and facilitate negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The UK plans to impose sanctions on Israeli settlements, drawing strong condemnation from Israeli officials who called for diplomatic retaliation. Russia affirmed Iran's role in regional stability and, along with North Korea, opened their first road bridge, signaling strengthening ties. Turkish President Erdogan stated that all countries pay the price for the war Israel started in the region. The IAEA Director General, Rafael Grossi, reported that Iran stated it would not cooperate on safeguards until a broader agreement is reached in ongoing negotiations.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are contradictions regarding casualty figures in southern Lebanon, with Lebanese media reporting 11 killed in Kfar Reman, including two children, while the IDF stated it is investigating claims of civilian harm. Iranian claims of sinking the USS Abraham Lincoln are contradicted by external reports of the carrier's presence in Thailand. Several unverified claims emerged from Iran, including the execution of Arfan Mirzaei, and reports of self-immolation in Hamedan and a suicide on Tehran's subway, which lack independent confirmation. Propaganda indicators are prevalent across various sources: Press TV consistently frames US/Israeli actions as "aggression," "war crimes," or "genocide"; Omid Dana expresses strong pro-Israel and anti-Iran regime sentiments; and N12 shows a pro-Israel stance, particularly concerning UK sanctions. There are reporting gaps regarding the specific extent of damage and casualties from Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities and the precise details of the US "diverted vessels" in the Strait of Hormuz.
